newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco bourse closes higher with banks leading.
newsitem.headline: Morocco bourse closes higher with banks leading.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed 0.86 percent higher on Wednesday boosted by Banque Commerciale du Maroc (BCM) and Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur (BMCE), brokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 638.33 points from 632.89 on Tuesday.

"The two banks accounted for 34 million dirhams of the overall volume traded on the official market," a broker at ABN-AMRO Finance said. BCM.CS gained 23 dirhams to 868 dirhams with 9,745 shares exchanged and BMCE rose 17 dirhams to 611 dirhams with 14,302 shares traded.
ONA Group rose 22 dirhams to 782 dirhams, while Societe Nationale d'Investissement fell four to 738.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir was up 10.3 dirhams at 356.35 dirham.
Steel mill Sonasid rose 16 dirhams to 563.

Brokerage Casablanca Finance Intermediation said on Wednesday that George Soros's sale of some of his Financiere Diwan stake was 1.8 times oversubscribed. Soros owned 12.7 percent of the company and sold 6.07 percent. About 500,000 shares were on offer at 330 dirhams each. Some 4,109 subscribers bought the 300,000 shares available to the general public, while 33 institutional investors, including eight from outside the country, acquired the remaining 200,000.
The total volume on the official market was 63 million, down from 97.6 million dirhams on Tuesday.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume jumped to 364 million dirhams from 63 million dirhams. Financiere Diwan accounted for 330 million dirhams of the total trading.
